metaDescription: Six tablet floor stands compared by base weight, height range and device fit, for hands-free viewing beside a bed, sofa or recliner.
introParagraphs: A floor stand lifts a tablet off your lap and parks it where your eyes are, which is why it suits bedside reading, sofa viewing and kitchen recipes. The catch is that a tall stand with an arm is a lever, so the weight of the base matters more than any other spec. The six floor stands here range from lightweight to a hefty 11 lb base.

The differences are easy to read in the numbers. The BluuSuuk top pick carries an 11 lb base, a second BluuSuuk uses a 6.6 lb base, and a SAMHOUSING model lists a 6 lb weight. In height, the Anautin adjusts from 35 to 64 inches, the standard SAMHOUSING from 27.5 to 53 inches, and the Houele holds screens up to 15.6 inches and adds a removable tray.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, weighing base weight, height range, device fit and how simple the stand is to build. Because floor stands cannot be carried easily, the right choice should fit where you sit most. The sections below help you match the stand to a bed, a sofa or a recliner.

products.name: BluuSuuk Tablet Floor Stand with 11 lb Base
products.description:
The BluuSuuk with the 11 lb base is the most stable floor stand in this roundup, and stability is the whole point of a floor stand. A double support structure and the heavy base keep the arm from pulling the stand over when it is fully extended. The swivel arm and flexible holder let you face the screen up, down, left or right, so it works for taking pictures, recording or just watching a show.

It makes sense for a spot that stays put, such as next to a bed or recliner. Space matters, since the base sits on the floor.

Setup is a one-time assembly, and cleaning is a wipe. Compared with the other BluuSuuk, whose base is 6.6 lb, the 11 lb version gives much more margin for a large tablet in a case. It is the stand to pick if tipping is your top worry.
products.bestFor: Heavy tablets and long arm extension where tipping is the main worry
pros: Handles hands-free viewing in any posture
cons: Too heavy to move between rooms

products.name: Anautin Adjustable 35 to 64 Inch Floor Stand
products.description:
The Anautin has the tallest range of any single-pole floor stand here, adjusting from 35 to 64 inches. That reach suits a standing user at a counter as well as someone reclining. The minimalist black metal frame looks tidy beside a bed or sofa and fits devices from 4.7 to 13 inches, including iPad Pro, Air and Mini, Kindle, Galaxy Tab and Switch.

The listing does not give a base weight in pounds, so you cannot judge its stability against the BluuSuuk numerically. A tall pole also magnifies any wobble at full extension, so use the lowest height that works.

Setup is simple and the frame wipes clean. Compared with the SAMHOUSING it extends higher, and compared with the BluuSuuk it is lighter in feel. It is a good pick for the person who moves between standing and sitting use.
products.bestFor: Switching between a standing cook, a sofa viewer and a bed viewer
pros: Lower cost than the heavy bases
cons: Tall pole wobbles more at full height

products.name: SAMHOUSING Adjustable Tablet Floor Stand
products.description:
The SAMHOUSING is the floor stand for people who want to follow a short manual and be done. It goes together without tools, adjusts from 27.5 to 53 inches, and rotates 360 degrees so switching between portrait and landscape is easy. It holds devices from 4.7 to 13 inches, which includes nearly every mainstream tablet.

It does take floor space and is not portable, so it works best as a permanent fixture beside a chair or bed. The listing does not state a base weight, so check stability by keeping the arm short.

Cleaning is a dry wipe. Compared with the 6 lb SAMHOUSING sibling, this one has a published height range and device range, whereas the sibling advertises a base weight. If clear specs and easy setup matter more than a heavy base, this is the one.
products.bestFor: An easy-to-build stand with clearly published height and device ranges
cons: Takes floor space and is not portable

products.name: SAMHOUSING Tablet Floor Stand with 6 lb Weight
products.description:
The listing says it was designed around complaints about similar stands that get shaky and tip over, and it is an overhead bed style with a stretchable arm. Height and angle are adjustable so you can reduce pressure on the neck.

A 6 lb base is lighter than the BluuSuuk's 11 lb, so it asks you to keep the arm short for large tablets. It is meant for light to medium loads such as a standard tablet without a heavy case. The finish and fit are what you would expect at the lowest cost tier.

Assembly is simple and cleaning is a wipe. Against the SAMHOUSING with the 53 inch pole, this version prioritizes base weight over published height range. It is the sensible pick for a first bedside stand.
products.bestFor: A first bedside stand with a stated base weight at a low cost
cons: Lighter base than the 11 lb BluuSuuk
Fewer published specs than its sibling

products.name: BluuSuuk Tablet Floor Stand with Double Weight Base
specs: Claw grip for iPhone or iPad
products.description:
This BluuSuuk model is the middle child of the family, with a base that was doubled from 3.3 lb to 6.6 lb after buyer feedback about tipping. Its arm extends over a bed, recliner or tabletop, and the claw grips an iPhone or iPad. The company acknowledges the earlier base was too light, which tells you the redesign was a response to a real problem.

The 6.6 lb base is still lighter than the 11 lb BluuSuuk, so a large tablet in a heavy case will lean harder on the arm. It suits phones and standard tablets more than big ones. Floor space is the usual cost.

Setup is quick and cleaning is a wipe. Compared with the 11 lb BluuSuuk it costs less and weighs less, and compared with the 6 lb SAMHOUSING it adds a little more base weight. It is a solid mid-range bedside stand.
products.bestFor: Phones and standard tablets above a bed or recliner
cons: Big cased tablets lean on the arm

products.name: Houele Floor Stand with Removable Tray

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Portable stand with Kindle and iPad support

products.description:
The Houele is the floor stand that adds a removable tray for a stylus, a phone, snacks or a remote. It adjusts in height and tilts the head through 360 degrees, which helps you find a comfortable angle. Devices from 4.7 to 15.6 inches fit, which is larger than most stands here.

The tray is useful but it adds a place to rest things that can topple, so keep liquids away from the tablet. The listing describes it as portable, but with a tray and a tall pole you should still treat it as a fixed piece. Base weight is not published.

Cleaning is a wipe of the tray and pole. Compared with the Anautin it handles larger screens and adds a tray, but its tall reach is not published as a number. It is a good choice for people who want a small side table built into the stand.
products.bestFor: Large tablets with a handy tray for small items
cons: Tray encourages clutter near the tablet

buyingCriteria.explanation: A floor stand's arm acts like a lever, so base weight sets tip resistance. The BluuSuuk lists 11 lb, its sibling lists 6.6 lb after doubling from 3.3 lb, and the SAMHOUSING lists 6 lb. Research puts roughly 4.5 lb as a minimum base for a full size iPad at full extension, so lighter bases deserve caution. Heavy cases add more load.

The Anautin runs 35 to 64 inches and the SAMHOUSING 27.5 to 53 inches. A screen held low pushes the neck forward, so raising it toward eye level helps. Check that the minimum height works for the chair or bed you use. A pole that is too tall at its lowest setting can be awkward.

The Houele handles up to 15.6 inches, while most others stop at 13 inches. A large iPad Pro in a case weighs more than the base assumes. Weigh your tablet with its case. Stay within the listing's range for safety.

The BluuSuuk models use a stretchable swivel arm, the SAMHOUSING rotates 360 degrees, and the Houele tilts its head 360 degrees. Joints must lock without drooping. A stiff, easy-to-lock joint is better than a loose one. Test the arm before relying on it.

The SAMHOUSING assembles without tools, and the other stands go together with simple steps. A stand that is hard to assemble is less likely to be set up properly. Look for a clear manual and few parts. Follow the manual closely.
The Houele adds a removable tray, and the BluuSuuk models use a claw grip. Extras add convenience but also clutter. Floor stands take space beside a bed or chair. Measure the spot before you buy.

howWeEvaluated.title: Base weight and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the published base weights, from the BluuSuuk's 11 lb to the SAMHOUSING's 6 lb. Stands that publish no weight were treated more cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared height ranges such as the Anautin's 35 to 64 inches and the SAMHOUSING's 27.5 to 53 inches. A wide range earns credit when the pole stays stable. Reach matters for bed and recliner use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Device fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked supported sizes, from the Houele's 15.6 inches to the 13 inch limit of the others. We also considered case weight. Fit determines whether the stand is usable for your tablet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Arm and adjustment
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the swivel, tilt and rotation options. A joint that locks firmly scored better. The strongest arm design is the BluuSuuk's, and the most basic is the SAMHOUSING sibling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed price tier against base weight and reach without quoting figures. The 6 lb SAMHOUSING is the lowest-cost pick, and the 11 lb BluuSuuk is the highest.

cards.label: Heavy base
cards.text: The 11 lb BluuSuuk and 6.6 lb BluuSuuk resist tipping and hold larger tablets. They cost more and are hard to move. Choose one if the tablet is big or the arm will be extended.

cards.label: Light base
cards.text: The 6 lb SAMHOUSING, SAMHOUSING 53 inch and Anautin are easier to shift and cost less, but they demand a short arm and a light device. Choose one for a standard tablet.

cards.label: Our recommendation
cards.text: Pick the 11 lb BluuSuuk if tipping worries you, and the SAMHOUSING 6 lb model if budget does.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a base weight above about 4.5 lb, an arm that reaches over the bed and a joint that locks. Press the base against the bed frame.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BluuSuuk 11 lb stand has the heaviest base, and the 6.6 lb BluuSuuk is a good mid-weight option. The 6 lb SAMHOUSING is the economical bedside choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you have a large tablet or want the arm fully extended. The 11 lb BluuSuuk base is the main thing the extra cost buys.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you have a light tablet and a short arm. The 6 lb SAMHOUSING and Anautin cover that at lower tiers.

faq.q: How do I choose between floor stands?
faq.a: Start with the heaviest tablet and case you plan to use. The 11 lb BluuSuuk suits large tablets, while the 6 lb SAMHOUSING suits light ones. Then check height range and setup. Pick the lightest stand that still holds your tablet steadily.

faq.q: How much do tablet floor stands cost?
faq.a: Prices run from the 6 lb SAMHOUSING at the lowest tier to the 11 lb BluuSuuk at the highest. The extra cost buys base weight and structure. For a light tablet a lower-cost stand is enough.

faq.q: Will a floor stand tip over?
faq.a: It can if the base is too light. Research puts roughly 4.5 lb as a minimum for a full size iPad at full extension, and the BluuSuuk models exceed that. Press the base against furniture, keep the arm short and avoid heavy cases. If it still tips, choose a heavier base.

faq.q: Do I need tools to assemble these?
faq.a: The SAMHOUSING assembles without tools by following a manual. Others use simple steps as well. Read the manual first and tighten each joint. A loose joint can droop.

faq.q: Can a floor stand hold a 15 inch device?
faq.a: The Houele lists support up to 15.6 inches. Most others stop at 13 inches. Check the weight limit too. Large devices need heavier bases.

faq.q: What height should I set it to?
faq.a: Raise the screen toward eye level so your neck stays upright. The Anautin reaches 64 inches and the SAMHOUSING 53 inches. Keep the pole low when you can, since taller settings wobble more.

faq.q: How do I clean a floor stand?
faq.a: Wipe the pole, arm and base with a dry or slightly damp cloth. Check joints and clamps for looseness from time to time. Keep liquids away from the tray on the Houele. Light care keeps it steady.
